To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) thrombocytocrit (TCP) is a simple and inexpensive method to measure platelet mass, (ii) TCP correlates well with the number of platelet transfusions required in patients with liver disease, (iii) TCP is a good predictor of platelet recovery after liver transplantation, (iv) the TCP is a good marker to assess the response to thrombopoietic agents and (v) TCP can be used to predict bleeding risk in patients undergoing invasive procedures.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is no evidence to support the use of any specific agent in the treatment of thrombocytopaenia in chronic liver disease, but that the use of recombinant erythropoietin is associated with a number of potential risks and benefits.
there is no clear evidence of the efficacy and safety of the use of platelet transfusions to improve the clinical outcome of patients with thrombocyt openia due to liver disease.

the evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine use of eltrombopag for the treatment of thrombocyclopenia in patients with chronic liver disease, including those with hepatitis C virus infection, who have failed to respond to other treatments, such as immunoglobulin or prednisone.

The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many factors that contribute to platelet transfusion practice, including patient characteristics, hospital characteristics, and the availability and cost of platelets.
the cost of platelet transfusions for patients with chronic liver disease is substantial, and that the use of eltrombopag is a cost-effective alternative to platelet transfusions.
